Increased TaDOG3 expression correlates with reduced pre-harvest sprouting, indicating its potential as a marker for seed dormancy.

Mechanistic insight into the progressive retinal atrophy disease in
dogs  via  pathway-based genome-wide association
analysis
result.summary: A genome-wide association study identified 1,114 markers linked to progressive retinal atrophy in dogs. Key associated pathways include apoptosis, cell adhesion, and axon guidance.

limitations: Nearest gene (LOC111091124) is uncharacterized in NCBI/dog with no known function, precluding mechanistic interpretation.
Variant is ~66kb outside the nearest gene's boundaries, reducing likelihood of direct regulatory/coding impact.

The reported genotype (A/G, compound_het) is unusual for a single locus where neither allele matches the reference (T) — this may reflect a genotyping/annotation artifact and could not be further resolved with available tools.
Evo2 deviation scores are small in magnitude but this is not a validated disease-probability metric — absence of a strong signal does not rule out functional effects not captured by the model.
No protein-level consequence could be assessed since the variant is non-coding/intergenic; no literature provided a protein-level (amino acid) annotation to justify ESM2 scoring.
Literature search did not return any species-specific (canine) functional studies of this exact locus.
